mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS 3-month moving average (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% for two consecutive months, labor market strength is interpreted as reducing uncertainty, which boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses below 50,000 and remains below for 2 months
failure_condition: A 20-day forward return regression with PAYEMS < 50,000 shows no significant positive coefficient (t < 1.96).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly rise in personal consumption expenditures (PCE) exceeding 0.5% of the prior month's value indicates accelerating demand, which typically precedes a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth > 0.5% of previous month's GDPC1
failure_condition: Over 30 consecutive 5-day windows, the 5-day forward return is not positively correlated with the subsequent month's GDPC1 growth (R < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Industrial Production index below 90 for three months suggests weakening manufacturing capacity, which often precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines for ≥3 months but SPX 20-day forward returns remain non-negative in 80% of such periods (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month CPIAUCSL prints above 233, it signals persistent price inflation expectations that, if sustained, typically depress equity valuations and drive negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, CPIAUCSL > 233 is never followed by a statistically significant negative 60-day forward return (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment rates above 6% indicate an economic slowdown, which often coincides with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as market uncertainty rises.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases for 2 consecutive months and remains above 6%
failure_condition: A 5-year rolling window shows no significant negative relationship between UNRATE > 6% persistence and subsequent SPX 20-day forward returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, one-time surge in monthly retail sales ( proxy: HOUST ) of more than 10% compared to the prior month creates temporary optimism about consumer demand, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly growth > 10% relative to prior month
failure_condition: Over 50 such events, the 5-day forward return is not significantly higher than the mean of non-shock periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial supply (INDPRO) and labor strength (PAYEMS) show simultaneous monthly increases above their 12-month averages, the combined effect amplifies market optimism and produces positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly growth > 12-month avg AND PAYEMS monthly growth > 12-month avg
failure_condition: In 100 matched INDPRO/PAYEMS double-move events, the 20-day forward return is not significantly higher than in non-matching events (p > 0.05).
